name: Val
about: Val is an established English short form of names including Valentine, Valerie and other names beginning with Val-. Through its connections with Valentine and Valerie, it can carry meanings associated with strength, health and vitality. Familiar, concise and comfortably used across genders, Val is a versatile gender-neutral name with a long naming history.

name: Vesper
about: Vesper comes from the Latin word for 'evening' and was also used in Roman tradition in connection with the evening star. The name has an atmospheric quality, evoking twilight and the first appearance of stars in the evening sky. Used across genders, Vesper is a distinctive gender-neutral name with an elegant celestial character.

name: Vanya
about: Vanya is a Russian and Bulgarian diminutive of Ivan or Ivana, ultimately related to the Hebrew name Yohanan and the idea of divine grace. Used for people of more than one gender in Slavic naming traditions, Vanya is familiar, warm and distinctly international. Its soft sound gives it an approachable gender-neutral character.

name: Vanja
about: Vanja is a South Slavic form related to Ivan and Ivana and ultimately to the Hebrew name Yohanan, traditionally understood through the meaning 'God is gracious.' It is used across genders in Croatian, Serbian and Slovene naming traditions, while also appearing in Scandinavian usage. Distinctive yet familiar, Vanja is a genuinely cross-cultural gender-neutral name.

name: Vân
about: Vân is a Vietnamese given name associated with the Sino-Vietnamese character 雲, meaning 'cloud.' The imagery connects the name with the sky, movement and the changing forms of nature. Used across genders in Vietnamese naming, Vân is a concise and lyrical gender-neutral choice whose diacritic preserves its cultural and linguistic identity.

name: Vanna
about: Vanna is a Khmer name associated with the Khmer word វណ្ណ, meaning 'colour,' ultimately connected with the Sanskrit word varṇa. The name carries an expressive association with colour and visual richness. Used across genders in Khmer naming, Vanna offers a distinctive Cambodian name with a bright and artistic character.

name: Vinh
about: Vinh is a Vietnamese given name derived from the Sino-Vietnamese element 榮, meaning 'glory' or honour. Its meaning conveys achievement, distinction and recognition. Used across genders in Vietnamese naming, Vinh is concise, strong and culturally rooted while remaining easy to discover internationally.

name: Vinnie
meaning: Short form of Vincent and related names
about: Vinnie is an English diminutive of Vincent and other names beginning with Vin-, with Vincent ultimately deriving from Latin vincens, meaning 'conquering' or 'prevailing.' Its affectionate form gives it a friendly and approachable character. Used across genders, Vinnie is a warm gender-neutral name with established English usage.

name: Vic
meaning: Short form of Victor or Victoria
about: Vic is an established English short form of Victor or Victoria, both ultimately derived from the Latin word victor, meaning 'conqueror' or 'winner.' Because it can shorten names traditionally associated with more than one gender, Vic has long functioned naturally across gender lines. Compact and familiar, it is a practical gender-neutral name with strong historical roots.

name: Valya
about: Valya is a Russian and Bulgarian diminutive associated with names such as Valentin, Valentina and related forms ultimately connected with Latin valens, meaning 'strong' or 'healthy.' Used across genders in Slavic naming traditions, Valya has an affectionate, melodic character while retaining a meaningful connection with strength and vitality.

name: Vivian
about: Vivian derives from the Latin name Vivianus, ultimately connected with Latin vivus, meaning 'alive.' It has historical masculine use and later became established as a feminine name in English-speaking countries, making it a longstanding cross-gender choice. Vivian is also used in Swedish, Norwegian and Danish naming traditions.

name: Vlada
about: Vlada is a Slavic short form associated with names containing the element meaning 'to rule' or 'to control.' Its gender associations vary by country: it is typically masculine in Serbia and feminine elsewhere, making it a useful example of a genuinely cross-gender Slavic name.

name: Vlasta
about: Vlasta is a Slavic name originally used as a short form of names containing an element associated with power, rule and sovereignty. It is used across genders in Czech, Slovak and South Slavic naming traditions, with its gender association varying between countries.

name: Ventura
about: Ventura is a Spanish name meaning 'fortune.' It can be a short form of Buenaventura or can be derived directly from the Spanish word ventura. Used across genders, Ventura has a distinctive Spanish character and an optimistic association with good fortune.

name: Veasna
about: Veasna is a Khmer name meaning 'fate' or 'destiny,' ultimately connected with Sanskrit vāsanā. Its meaning gives the name a strong association with life's path and what is meant to unfold. Used across genders, Veasna adds a distinctive Cambodian and Southeast Asian presence to the collection.

name: Vũ
about: Vũ is a Vietnamese name whose meaning depends on the Sino-Vietnamese character used. Possible characters connect it with ideas including military or martial qualities, rain, and feathers. This makes Vũ a compact name with several distinct cultural and symbolic possibilities.

name: Voski
about: Voski is an Armenian name meaning 'gold.' Its precious-metal meaning gives it associations with value, warmth and radiance. Used across genders, Voski provides a distinctive Armenian option and a memorable nature-inspired symbolic name.

name: Vəfa
about: Vəfa is an Azerbaijani name meaning 'loyalty,' ultimately derived from an Arabic root associated with fulfilling a promise or living up to one's word. Its virtue meaning gives it a clear association with faithfulness, trust and integrity.

name: Vieno
about: Vieno is a rare Finnish name meaning 'gentle.' Its soft meaning and Finnish origin give it a calm, understated character. Although uncommon, it is established as a name usable across genders and adds a distinctive Nordic option to the collection.

name: Vaska
about: Vaska is a Slavic diminutive with different derivational routes across the region. In Russian it can derive from Vasiliy, while in Macedonian and Bulgarian it can be associated with Vasilija. These masculine and feminine connections give Vaska a strong cross-gender character within Slavic naming traditions.
